subject: Review/approve: Optimization Suggestions (Console) beta launch brief + disclaimers + enablement plan
body:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 5, 2026 at 9:12 AM
Subject: Review/approve: Optimization Suggestions (Console) beta launch brief + disclaimers + enablement plan
Attachments: Optimization_Suggestions_Beta_Launch_Brief_v3.docx

Can you both do a fast pass on the attached launch brief v3 today and reply with either:
1) “Approved” or
2) “Approved w/ edits” + the specific edits

Two areas I want us aligned on before we circulate wider:
- Disclaimers/copy: estimated savings (no guarantees), what “risk” means (perf/reliability only), and what we do/don’t do in beta (no auto-apply).
- Enablement plan: per-org feature flag, who can turn it on/off, and rollback expectations.

Timing: trying to lock by EOD so we can start enabling the first cohort next week.

Thanks,
Marissa

—
Marissa Cole
Product (Console & Rollouts)
Redwood Inference



From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 5, 2026 at 11:03 AM
Subject: Re: Review/approve: Optimization Suggestions (Console) beta launch brief + disclaimers + enablement plan

Approved w/ edits (enablement/ops sections):

1) Enablement ownership / controls
- Current text says “Support can enable for customers.” I’d recommend we tighten to: only Eng on-call (or a named eng group) can flip the flag during the first week, then we can expand once we’re confident.
- We should explicitly say it’s per-org (not per-project) for beta, since the UI entry point is org-scoped.

2) Rollback criteria (please add)
- Add a short bullet list for when we roll back/disallow new org enables:
  - suggestions API p95 > budget for 30m
  - sustained 5xx above threshold
  - compute job lag causing stale estimates beyond the “stale as of” window

3) Staleness expectations (copy tweak)
- In the “How it works” section, can we add one sentence: “Estimates are computed from recent telemetry and may be up to <N hours> behind live traffic.”

4) Permissions
- In brief we should state: viewing Suggestions requires Optimize suggestions read permission (RBAC). (I know we’re implementing it; launch brief should call it out so we’re not surprised by access requests.)

Everything else looks good.

Dylan

—
Dylan Brooks
Engineering (Console & Tooling)
Redwood Inference



From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 5, 2026 at 1:27 PM
Subject: Re: Review/approve: Optimization Suggestions (Console) beta launch brief + disclaimers + enablement plan
Attachments: disclaimer-copy-options.txt

Approved w/ edits (disclaimers + estimator language). I added some suggested copy in the attached.

Key requested changes:

1) “Estimated savings” language (tighten)
- Replace “estimated savings” in the headline section with “estimated savings based on recent telemetry” (keeps us honest).
- In the FAQ, explicitly say: “Estimates are not a guarantee and may differ from billing due to traffic mix changes, retries, and pricing plan differences.”

2) Risk definition (avoid security interpretation)
- Suggest using: “Risk reflects likelihood of increased latency or reduced reliability if you apply the recommendation.”
- Add a one-liner: “Risk does not refer to security/compliance risk.”

3) Beta scope (restate plainly)
- We should say it twice: “This beta only includes batching and caching suggestions. It does not include quantization recommendations.”

4) Guardrails / safe application
- In the “How to apply” section, add: “Apply changes via a rollout (canary/gradual) and monitor latency/error rate. Do not apply globally without verifying on your critical routes.”

5) Telemetry requirements (make crisp)
- Call out that customers need sufficient traffic + latency/cost attribution metrics enabled; otherwise they may see “insufficient telemetry.”

All edits are compatible with current v0 estimator (conservative positioning).

Aditya

—
Aditya Rao
Product (Optimize)
Redwood Inference



From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 5, 2026 at 3:06 PM
Subject: Re: Review/approve: Optimization Suggestions (Console) beta launch brief + disclaimers + enablement plan

Thanks — all makes sense.

On Dylan’s points:
- Agree on tighter enablement ownership for week 1. I’ll update to “Engineering on-call / named eng group” and explicitly state per-org.
- Will add rollback criteria bullets and a staleness line (I’ll use “up to 24 hours behind” unless you feel strongly we should commit to smaller).
- Will add the RBAC callout.

On Aditya’s points:
- I’ll adopt your “recent telemetry” qualifier and the billing caveat.
- Updating the risk definition to explicitly exclude security/compliance.
- Repeating beta scope (batching/caching only) in Overview + FAQ.
- Adding rollout guidance and telemetry requirements.

I’ll incorporate and send v4 for a final skim before I circulate.

Marissa



From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 5, 2026 at 5:46 PM
Subject: Re: Review/approve: Optimization Suggestions (Console) beta launch brief + disclaimers + enablement plan

v4 is live (same Drive link) with the edits we discussed:
- Enablement: per-org flag; limited to eng group during week 1
- Rollback criteria + staleness callout
- RBAC permission callout
- Disclaimers: “recent telemetry,” no guarantees, billing deltas caveat
- Risk definition clarified (perf/reliability only; not security)
- Beta scope restated (batching/caching only)
- “Apply via rollout” guidance

Unless either of you spot an issue tonight, I’m treating this as approved and will circulate tomorrow morning.

Marissa
